features.gap: Only create/drop/drop_and_create derived from the model's own columns (not a free-form table definition). No `if_not_exists`, `force: :cascade`, `temporary`, `comment`, `id: :uuid/false`, composite PK options, or `drop_table if_exists/cascade` options. No indexes, FKs, or check constraints at create time. Spec asserts exact SQL only for the active adapter.

features.feature: Micrate integration — versioned SQL migration files (Up/Down)
features.gap: No Micrate reference in src/ or spec/; only docs. Versioned files, up/down, and the tracking table are wholly external. Grant offers no way to run a Crystal migration class or to call Micrate from a Grant API.
Hand-written SQL Up/Down only. No `change` with automatic inverse, no `reversible`/`revert`/`up_only`, and no IrreversibleMigration error.
CLI lives in Amber/Micrate outside this repo. Grant provides no task API (create/drop database, migrate, rollback, status, seed) that a CLI can call, and no spec exists.

Maps only Bool, Float32/64, Int32/64, String, Time, UUID, created_at/updated_at (+ PG arrays). No mapping for Int8/Int16, Decimal/BigDecimal with precision/scale, Bytes, JSON::Any/jsonb, Date, Enum, Time precision, or text vs string with limit. These raise at migrate time. Spec asserts the SQL only for the current adapter.
No dump, no load, no schema file format, and no introspection layer to build one from.

No index DSL. The model-based Migrator emits no indexes or unique constraints, even for `unique` columns. Missing options: unique, name, where (partial), using, order, opclass, include, expression indexes, algorithm concurrently, if_not_exists, length. No index introspection.
No FK DDL from Grant, no `references`/`foreign_key: true` in table definitions, no on_delete/on_update/deferrable/validate options, no introspection. Model `belongs_to` does not emit an FK.
No DSL, no introspection, no `validate:` option, no `t.check_constraint`.

Only Crystal literal defaults (String, Number, Bool, nil) become SQL DEFAULT. No SQL-expression defaults (`default: -> { "now()" }`, `gen_random_uuid()`), no `change_column_default`, and non-literal Crystal defaults silently produce no DDL default.
Only a convention (a Crystal script); no `Grant::Seed` runner, no `db/seeds.cr` lookup, no idempotent-seed helper, and no spec.
No Grant code reads or writes schema_migrations or ar_internal_metadata (environment protection). No current_version, status, pending check, or per-database migration paths.

features.feature: Encryption migration helpers (data migration for encrypted columns)
features.gap: rotate_encryption is exercised on SQLite (8 examples pass). encrypt_column, decrypt_column and generate_migration have no spec. The helpers loop with `limit/offset` and `save!` per row (offset paging skips rows if the predicate changes), and no PG/MySQL run.
Scaffolding lives in the separate Amber CLI project; nothing in Grant's src/ or specs. No name-parsing (AddXToY -> add_column) inside Grant.

features.feature: alter_table / change_column / add_column at runtime via Grant DSL
features.gap: No ALTER TABLE DSL of any kind (add/remove/change column, null, default, change_table bulk). SQLite needs a table rebuild for change_column.
No rename_table DSL (which in AR also renames the pk sequence and indexes).
No rename_column/rename_index; AR also renames default-named indexes on column rename.
No join-table DDL helper (name derivation from two tables, FK columns, optional index).

features.feature: references / belongs_to columns in migrations (add_reference, remove_reference, polymorphic)
features.gap: No reference helper; polymorphic `_type`/`_id` pair, index, and FK creation must be hand-written.
Model `timestamps` yields created_at/updated_at in create_sql (VARCHAR on SQLite), but there is no add_timestamps/remove_timestamps or `precision:` option, and no NOT NULL on the timestamp columns.

features.feature: Column options: null, limit, precision, scale, comment, collation, array
features.gap: Nullability is derived from Crystal nilability, and `column_type:` allows a verbatim SQL type. There are no `limit`, `precision`, `scale`, `comment`, or `collation` options. Arrays are PG-only via type table.
No comment DDL (PG COMMENT ON, MySQL COMMENT clause; SQLite unsupported).

features.feature: Introspection: table_exists?, column_exists?, columns, tables, primary_key, indexes, foreign_keys
features.gap: No catalog introspection (grep of src/ finds only schema_tenant's schemata query). Blocks schema dump, idempotent migrations, and model/table drift checks.
Grant's columns are declared at compile time in the model, so there is no runtime column cache to reset or dump. A drift check between model and DB would need introspection (see introspection row).
features.not_applicable_reason: Ruby lazily reads columns from the DB and caches them; Grant declares columns at compile time, so a runtime column cache does not exist. The compile-time schema is the source of truth.

features.feature: Migration class: up/down/change with versioned class ([8.0] compat)
features.gap: No Migration base class or per-version compatibility layer; migrations are SQL files for external Micrate. Compat layers (ActiveRecord::Migration::Compatibility) are Rails-history specific.

features.feature: MigrationContext operations: migrate to version, rollback(step), redo, up/down(version), forward, status
features.gap: None present in Grant; must go through Micrate CLI.
No migration runner, so no per-migration transaction wrapping and no opt-out (needed for CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on PG). MySQL does not support transactional DDL.

features.feature: Migration output and helpers: say, say_with_time, announce, suppress_messages
features.gap: No migration runner output layer; could reuse Grant::Log.
No detection of pending migrations at boot/in specs and no auto load of the test schema.
No metadata table storing environment, so destructive tasks (drop/reset) in production are not blocked. `Migrator#drop_and_create` is unguarded.
No DDL. Migrator never emits UNIQUE, even for validates_uniqueness_of fields.

features.feature: Composite primary keys and primary key options in table creation
features.gap: Migrator handles a single `primary: true` column (Int auto or UUID/String) and raises without one. Composite PK models exist (src/grant/composite_primary_key.cr) but the Migrator emits a single-column PK only; `id: false` tables (join tables) unsupported.

No view DDL or view-backed model helpers; `view_exists?`/`views` introspection absent. Deferred: Low value, and needs PG-specific refresh semantics. Raw execute covers it until the DDL DSL (M02b) is stable.

features.feature: PostgreSQL enum types, extensions, and custom column types (create_enum, enable_extension, hstore, citext, jsonb, inet, ltree, money)
features.gap: No DDL for enums or extensions; type table lacks these types. `column_type:` verbatim works as a workaround.

No DDL for generated columns; must use verbatim `column_type:`. Deferred: Low value and overlaps the Infrastructure virtual-column row. Verbatim column_type: works as a workaround. Do both together later.

features.feature: execute (raw DDL inside a migration) and schema-qualified table names
features.gap: Model.exec works for raw SQL (out of scope). Missing: a migration-scoped `execute` that respects the runner's connection and dry run, plus schema-qualified DDL names across all DSL calls (quote handles dotted names).

features.feature: Multi-database migrations (per-connection migrations_paths, db:migrate:primary, connection-specific tasks)
features.gap: Grant has named connections and sharding, but no migration runner targets one by name, and there is no per-connection schema_migrations. Schema-tenant (PG search_path) migrations across tenants are also absent.

features.feature: Database tasks: create/drop database, purge, structure dump (structure.sql), setup/reset/prepare, truncate_all
features.gap: No Grant API; Micrate/Amber CLI does create/drop only. No structure dump/load, purge, `db:prepare`, `db:reset`, or `truncate_all`.

features.feature: Schema format configuration (:ruby vs :sql) and db:schema:load for fresh environments
features.gap: Depends on the schema dump row; nothing to select or load.
No migration runner and no advisory-lock helper in Grant, so two deploy nodes can run the same DDL concurrently.

features.feature: Migration file generator naming conventions (AddXToY, CreateXs parse, timestamped versions)
features.gap: Covered only inside the external Amber CLI row; no attribute parsing DSL in Grant.

features.feature: Metaprogrammed migration lookup: Migration.method_missing forwarding to connection, and ActiveRecord::Migration.[] compatibility shims
features.not_applicable_reason: Rails forwards unknown migration methods to the connection through method_missing, and keeps version shims for Ruby-era default changes. Grant has no legacy versions to shim and would define typed methods.

features.gap: Core encrypt/decrypt, deterministic lookup, nil handling and rotation work. Cipher is AES-256-CBC+HMAC, not AES-GCM. Storage uses a separate <attr>_encrypted column instead of transparent same-name column. Only String attributes. Missing options: previous:, ignore_case:, downcase:, compress:, key_provider:, encryptor:, message_serializer:, per-attribute support_unencrypted_data:. Rotation specs are SQLite-only.

DSL, detection, key tuple helpers and find/exists? signatures exist (12 passing SQLite examples, config only). Persistence is unimplemented: composite_primary_key/transactions.cr is an empty TODO module, so create/update/destroy/reload rely on the single-key path. No spec inserts and reads back a composite-key row. Missing AR parts: find with array of tuples, where(id: [[a,b],...]), to_param/id as Array, associations with composite foreign keys, primary_key: [..] on belongs_to/has_many.

pg.cr maps Array(String/Int/Float/Bool) to TEXT[]/INT[]/etc. and type.cr has from_rs for arrays. No spec covers array round-trip, and the cited specs are JSON and numeric converters, not arrays. Query operators (ANY, @>, &&, array_length), array_append/remove helpers and UUID/Time arrays are absent.

Grant::Serializers::JSONB class exists but stores plain JSON text; specs are converter unit specs only, no DB round-trip or PG jsonb column. Missing: native jsonb column type in migrations, operators (->, ->>, @>, ?, #>), where(data: {a: 1}) containment, store_accessor, in-place mutation dirty tracking.

Only auto-generation of a v4 UUID on save is specced. Not proven: reload/round-trip through the DB, find/find_by by UUID string or UUID, UUID primary key, invalid-string casting, PG native uuid column vs CHAR(36) on MySQL/SQLite, gen_random_uuid() DB default.

retry_attempts and retry_delay properties exist on the pool config struct in connection_registry.cr but nothing reads them (grep finds only the declarations). Only failover_retry_attempts is used, by replica failover. No retry loop around connect or query on connection loss, and no spec on any adapter.
No YAML fixture loader, no label-to-id hashing, no fixture accessors, no transactional-test wrapper.
No adapter API for advisory locks. Rationale for n.a. (not core) is not a Ruby-metaprogramming reason; AR ships these as adapter methods used by the migrator.

features.feature: QueryLogs with context tags (SQL comment injection)
features.gap: annotate exists per query, but no global tag config, no fiber-local context, no automatic prepend of model/controller/action/job tags.

Column name lock_version is hard-coded in src/grant/locking/optimistic.cr (declares column and builds the WHERE). No locking_column override, no automatic activation when a lock_version column exists, no lock_optimistically toggle.
No API to scope find/update/destroy/reload by multiple columns while keeping a single-column primary key (for example a sharded or tenant-partitioned key).

Column metadata is compile-time macro state (column_for_attribute exists) but there is no runtime introspection of the actual DB: no tables/columns/indexes/foreign_keys query API, no table_exists?/column_exists?, no dump and load of a cache file, no drift check between declared and actual columns.

features.feature: Encryption: previous: schemes for key/scheme migration
features.gap: Only one active key; rotation is a batch re-encrypt helper (MigrationHelpers.rotate_encryption), not read-with-old, write-with-new. No multiple primary keys and no per-attribute previous schemes, so a rotation requires a maintenance window.
Not supported by the encrypts macro; case-insensitive deterministic lookup requires the caller to downcase manually.
No compression before encrypting; large text columns are stored uncompressed.

features.feature: Encryption: support_unencrypted_data and per-attribute plaintext fallback
features.gap: Config.support_unencrypted_data exists and EncryptedAttribute#decrypt honors it, but the macro-generated getter calls Grant::Encryption.decrypt, which does not; no spec exercises the flag. Also no per-attribute override and no way to query plaintext + ciphertext together during migration.

features.feature: Encryption: transparent same-name column and non-String attribute types
features.gap: encrypts creates a virtual String accessor over a <attr>_encrypted column; the original column name is not usable, where(email: ...) is not rewritten, and Int/Time/JSON values cannot be encrypted.

features.feature: Encryption context and record helpers (encrypted_attribute?, ciphertext_for, encrypt, decrypt, without_encryption, protecting_encrypted_data)
features.gap: encrypted_attributes registry exists but there is no instance ciphertext_for/encrypted_attribute?/encrypt/decrypt, and no scoped blocks to disable or pin encryption (keys, encryptor) per fiber.

features.feature: Encryption: pluggable key_provider, encryptor, message_serializer, AES-GCM cipher
features.gap: KeyProvider is a concrete class with class-level state. Cipher is CBC+HMAC with a custom byte layout, so ciphertext is not interoperable with Rails data. No envelope-encryption provider (KMS) and no swappable encryptor. Deferred: Changing the cipher or payload layout breaks existing ciphertext. Needs a versioned payload design and a rotation plan first. Rails-compatible messages are a separate decision.

features.feature: Encryption: filter_parameters and inspect masking of encrypted attributes
features.gap: No filter_attributes; grep finds no inspect override on models. Plaintext appears in inspect, logs of bound values and exceptions.

features.feature: Instrumentation notifications (sql / transaction / instantiation / strict_loading_violation events with payload)
features.gap: Only Log sub-loggers. No subscribe API with structured payload (sql, binds, name, duration, connection, cached, async), so APMs and query counters cannot hook in typed.

features.feature: Verbose query logs (source location of SQL) and log tags with binds
features.gap: SQL log shows query with colorized params but no calling file:line, no query-name label (User Load), no cached-hit marker.

features.feature: Optimistic locking on destroy/touch, locking_enabled?, and stale-record refresh
features.gap: StaleObjectError is raised on update only (optimistic.cr); destroy and touch do not include lock_version in their WHERE, so a stale destroy succeeds. No locking_enabled?, no automatic lock_version increment on touch.

features.feature: Pessimistic lock! raises on unsaved changes
features.gap: lock! just calls reload_with_lock, silently discarding unsaved attribute changes; AR raises to prevent that data loss (unless lock! is given a lock clause on a clean record). Also no lock: option on association reload.
No lock preventing two processes from running migrations at once on PG or MySQL.
No Hash(String, String?) column type, no migration type or operators. Deferred: Low value, PG only, and JSONB covers the main use.

features.feature: Database-specific types: PostgreSQL ranges, network (inet/cidr/macaddr), interval, native enum, citext
features.gap: Only PG::Interval appears in the adapter's allowed type list and no spec covers it. No Range(T,T) column mapping, no Socket::IPAddress column, no PG CREATE TYPE enum mapping or citext. Deferred: Effort L, low value, and range bound normalization makes dirty tracking risky. Take individual types on demand.

features.feature: Test assertions for queries (assert_queries_count, assert_no_queries, assert_queries_match)
features.gap: QueryStats/N1Detector record queries but there is no Spec-friendly helper that counts or matches SQL inside a block and fails with the captured SQL list. Depends on the notification layer for a clean hook.
Grant relies on external Micrate and the Amber CLI for these operations; no Grant-level programmatic create/drop/purge/prepare API and no structure-dump load.

features.feature: Integration cache keys and to_param (cache_key, cache_version, collection_cache_key)
features.gap: No cache_key/cache_version derived from updated_at and no relation-level collection_cache_key; no to_param override hook.

features.feature: Marshal/YAML coders and Ruby-only serialization internals (Marshal.dump of records, YAMLColumn, encode_with)
features.not_applicable_reason: Ruby Marshal/Psych object-graph serialization has no Crystal analog; JSON/YAML columns are covered by serialized_column.

features.gap: Blankness differs from AR Object#blank?: src/grant/validators.cr presence block treats Bool false and an empty Hash as present (AR fails both; false fails presence in AR). No allow_blank: option (only allow_nil:, which AR does not document for presence). on: takes one symbol, not an array. message: cannot be a Proc/Symbol.

Row text is covered (scope single/multi, case_sensitive, allow_nil, self-exclusion in uniqueness_spec.cr) but allow_blank: has no spec, and AR options conditions: (lambda scope on the uniqueness query), index_errors:, and validating against a scope named as an association are absent. The case_sensitive: false path builds raw `LOWER(col) = LOWER(?)` with an unquoted column name. Not run per-adapter (SQLite only here).

All failing constraints collapse into one combined message (e.g. 'must be greater than 0 and an integer') carrying a single error code; AR adds one error per failed constraint with its own type (:greater_than, :not_an_integer ...). Bounds must be compile-time literals: no Symbol (other attribute) or Proc operand for greater_than/less_than/equal_to/other_than (AR supports both). No spec for equal_to, other_than, less_than_or_equal_to, allow_blank, in:. only_numeric string-before-typecast semantics are replaced by ConversionError.

features.feature: Unified validates macro (AR style: validates :field, presence: true, length: {min:2})
features.gap: No `validates` macro. Each validator needs its own macro call; no per-attribute option hash, no shared if:/unless:/on:/allow_nil/allow_blank/strict/message defaults across sub-validators, no custom-validator lookup by key (`my: true` -> MyValidator).

Grant::Validator/EachValidator exist and validates_with forwards ctor args, but: validator is constructed with args, not an AR-style `options` hash (no `options[:foo]`, no default `options` reader); Validator#validate takes an untyped record (no `Grant::Validator(T)` generic); EachValidator reads values via `record.to_h[attribute]` snapshot (returns nil for non-column attributes, allocates a hash per attribute per run); `validates_each` has no `allow_nil`/`allow_blank` handling; a validator error from `validate` is not tied to the validator's type code.

Specs cover on: :create/:update only. Divergences from AR: (1) bare `valid?` runs ALL validators including on: :update ones on a new record (contexts_spec.cr 'running without context runs all validators' pins this); AR defaults context to :create for new records and :update for persisted ones. (2) on: accepts one symbol, not an array. (3) No spec for user-defined contexts on: :custom. (4) save/save!/create do not accept context:.

features.feature: Conditional validations (if:, unless: as Symbol method references)
Errors API (add, [], full_messages, where, of_type, include?, attribute_names, group_by_attribute, merge!, to_hash, to_json)
features.gap: Listed methods exist and 62 examples pass, but semantics diverge: of_type(attr, message : String) matches on MESSAGE while AR of_type(attr, type) matches the type symbol; where(attr) has no type/options filter; to_hash takes no full_messages arg; to_json emits [{field,message}] not AR's {attr => [messages]}; add() takes no options and cannot generate messages from a type symbol; merge! copies Error references (shared mutable objects).

Errors#details now exists and returns {"attr" => [{:error => type}]} with :invalid fallback (parity_spec.cr 'errors.details (typed codes)', 26 examples pass on SQLite). Remaining: no options in the detail hash (AR: {error: :too_short, count: 3}, {error: :greater_than, count: 0, value: -1}); details keys are Strings not Symbols; only some validators pass a type (numericality reports only the first constraint code); no `Error#details`/`Error#type` typed options; errors added by validates_with need explicit type: or fall back to :invalid.

features.feature: strict: option on validators (raises instead of adding to errors)
features.gap: No strict: option. Depends on Grant::ValidationError (ActiveModel::StrictValidationFailed) existing; neither present.

features.feature: Full lifecycle callbacks (before/after save, create, update, destroy, after_initialize, after_find, before/after_validation, after_touch)
Callback halting via abort! (equivalent to AR throw :abort)
Conditional callbacks (if:, unless: on lifecycle callbacks)
after_rollback fires on explicit transaction rollback
Callback ordering (multiple callbacks on same event)

features.gap: Each event is publicly callable (`item.before_create`, spec 'manually triggered' passes as written) which runs the before/after chain for that one event. Still missing: `run_callbacks(:save) { ... }` wrapping a block between before and after chains (incl. around callbacks and halting return value), and a symbol-dispatched runtime form.

Implemented as a before_validation hook only, so values are normalized on valid?/save, not on assignment (AR normalizes in the attribute setter and on read of existing values). Only String-valued attributes; one attribute per call (no `normalizes :a, :b`); no with: lambda form (block only); no apply_to_nil:; no Model.normalize_value_for(:attr, value); where/find_by conditions are not normalized (AR normalizes query values); save(validate: false) skips normalization; if: option is not in AR.

valid?(context: sym) is a keyword arg (not positional `valid?(:custom)`), and every spec uses only :create/:update. No spec for a user-defined context (`on: :publish` + `valid?(context: :publish)`), for on: arrays, or for save(context: :custom).

No global API to register a block that runs after the outermost transaction commits (or immediately when none is open). The needed hook (Grant::Transaction.enqueue_pending_callback) exists internally for record commit callbacks.

save! raises Grant::RecordNotSaved whose message is only `errors.first.message` (no 'Validation failed: Name can't be blank, ...' full_messages). There is no distinct RecordInvalid, so callers cannot rescue validation failures separately from callback aborts. By code reading (not run), RecordNotSaved.new calls errors.first, which would raise Enumerable::EmptyError when a callback aborted with no validation errors.
No validate!/validate(context) alias; grep of src/ finds none.

save derives :create/:update itself (src/grant/transactions.cr) and accepts only validate:/skip_timestamps:. No context: kw, no validation_context reader available to custom validators/callbacks during a run.

features.feature: on: array of contexts and on: for before_validation/after_validation callbacks
features.gap: `on:` on validators is a single symbol; before_validation/after_validation macros accept only if:/unless: (src/grant/callbacks.cr), no on: :create/:update.

features.feature: Multi-attribute form for every validates_*_of macro
features.gap: Only validates_presence_of, uniqueness, absence, associated, each accept *fields. numericality, format, length/size, inclusion, exclusion, comparison, confirmation, acceptance, email, url take a single field, so `validates_length_of :a, :b, maximum: 10` does not compile.

features.feature: Error message generation from type symbol, message: as Symbol/Proc, errors.add(attr, :type, **options)
features.gap: Messages are hard-coded English strings at macro expansion. errors.add(:name, :blank) does not compile (message is String); `message:` on validators must be a String literal, not a Symbol key or `->(object, data)` proc; no %{count} interpolation.

features.feature: Errors extras (delete, added?, of_type by type, messages_for, full_message, import/copy!, objects, uniq!, count by attribute)
features.gap: Absent from src/grant/errors.cr: delete(attr, type=nil), added?(attr, type, **opts), messages_for(attr), full_message(attr, msg), import(error, attribute:), copy!(other), objects, uniq!, generate_message, errors.messages Hash accessor, errors.to_hash(true).

features.feature: ActiveModel::Error object API (attribute, type, options, raw_type, message, detail, full_message, strict_match?)
features.gap: Grant::Error has field, message, type; missing options, attribute alias, raw_type, detail, full_message(instance), match?(attr, type, **opts). to_s capitalizes only the first letter of the raw column name (no humanize: 'first_name' becomes 'First_name').
No locale lookup, no Model.human_attribute_name, no per-model/per-attribute message overrides, no format template ('%{attribute} %{message}').

features.feature: validates_each block form (validates_each :a, :b do |record, attr, value|)
features.gap: validates_each exists but requires with: naming an EachValidator subclass; the block form used in most Rails code is not supported, and allow_nil/allow_blank are ignored.

features.feature: Validator reflection (validators, validators_on, validate callbacks introspection)
features.gap: __validators_for_validation is internal; no public list of validators per attribute, no kind/options metadata, so form builders and API docs cannot derive maxlength/required.
Not in CALLBACK_NAMES (src/grant/callbacks.cr) or the commit dispatch in src/grant/commit_callbacks.cr.

Callback macros take only if:/unless:; after_rollback fires regardless of the action while AR after_rollback supports on:. Also AR dedups commit callbacks when the same record is saved several times in one transaction; not verified in Grant.

features.feature: Callback conditions as arrays and combined if:+unless: lists
features.gap: Callback and validator macros accept a single SymbolLiteral or proc; an array like `if: [:a?, ->(r) { ... }]` is not handled (callbacks.cr and the validator prologues test only is_a?(SymbolLiteral)).
CALLBACKS entries are always appended; no prepend: (used by dependent: :destroy ordering guidance in Rails).

features.feature: skip_callback / set_callback / define_callbacks / reset_callbacks (custom callback chains)
features.gap: No way to skip an inherited callback in a subclass or define new callback chains; runtime per-call skipping is impossible with compile-time chains. Callback chain is a compile-time constant, so run-time mutation is Ruby-metaprogramming-shaped. Deferred: Effort L, low value, and compile-time chains make Ruby-style runtime mutation a poor fit. Revisit after CB01.

features.feature: Callback objects (before_save MyCallback.new / class with before_save(record))
features.gap: Callbacks accept a method Symbol or a block only; no object with a before_save(record) protocol for shared, testable callback classes. Deferred: Low value. A method Symbol or block already covers the use; the callback-object protocol adds compile-time surface for little benefit.

features.feature: Model.normalize_value_for and normalization on query conditions
features.gap: No public normalize_value_for(attr, value); where(email: " A@X.COM ") and find_by do not normalize the search value while AR does.

Grant's database: is a default connection name and role mapping lives in a separate config: argument, whereas AR takes database: {writing:, reading:}. Connection names are not validated against the registry (fails late at first query), and pools still need separate establish_connection calls. No default_shard / shard_keys / sharded? introspection. shard_config from connects_to(shards:) is honored by plain models, but models using Sharding::Model ignore it (they use ShardManager). Subclass inheritance is a copy at declaration time only. Existing spec uses fake postgres URLs as connection names, so it proves only the config maps.

Cited evidence (prevent_writes_spec) only covers prevent_writes. Role/shard/database switching is only asserted as context values, never as the actual adapter chosen. Probe: on a Sharding::Model model, connected_to(shard: other) was ignored (count returned rows from all shards / wrong shard) because Sharding::Model.adapter reads ShardManager.current_shard, not the ConnectionContext. database: takes a String, not a role hash. No connected_to_many, no connected_to?(role:, shard:), no prohibit_shard_swapping.

AR makes connected_to(role: :reading) automatically prevent writes (ReadOnlyError). Probe: Todo.connected_to(role: :reading) { Todo.create! } succeeds in Grant. Default role is :primary while config keys use :writing, so role names are inconsistent; no configurable reading_role/writing_role.

Only pool_size, initial_pool_size, checkout_timeout, retry_attempts, retry_delay are forwarded as crystal-db URL params. No idle_timeout, reaping, max_age, min_connections, keepalive. Exhaustion/checkout timeout is not tested and is testable on SQLite (pool_size 1, hold a connection, expect timeout); checkout timeout surfaces as a raw DB pool error, not a Grant error.

Monitor is periodic (default 30 s), so a failure is detected late and recovery needs a later successful check; tests run with test_mode so the background fiber never runs in specs. No on-demand Adapter#active?/verify!/reconnect! API. Model-level health_check_interval class_property is inert (only ConnectionSpec's is used). No PostgreSQL failure/recovery evidence.

features.feature: Read replica load balancing (multiple replicas, strategies)
features.gap: configure_connection(load_balancing_strategy:) does not compile (expands to undefined self.load_balancing_strategy=; confirmed). LeastConnectionsStrategy#release_connection is never called, so counts only grow and it degrades to rotation. Multiple replicas can be added only by registering the same database/role/shard key... registry keys are db:role so a second reader with the same key overwrites the first; the registry cannot register two readers for one database without distinct names. No weighted strategy. Fixtures are SQLite.

By code reading, get_adapter skips the health check for role :reading: with an explicit reading role and one unhealthy sole replica it returns the unhealthy adapter instead of falling back to the writer. Model failover_retry_attempts is an inert property (no retry loop uses it). Fallback for :writing only tries the :primary role key. No PostgreSQL evidence.

HashResolver uses String#hash, which Crystal seeds randomly per process: crystal eval printed "1".hash.abs % 4 as 0, 2, 1 on three runs. Shard assignment therefore changes on every restart and would misroute persisted data. Only shard counts 1,2,3,4,8,16 are supported (symbols cannot be built dynamically). Specs run on virtual adapters that record SQL, so no spec restarts a process or reads real routed rows.

TimeRangeResolver only converts Time bounds into string ranges of a composite ID format (%Y_%m_%d_...), so it works only for String keys in that layout; a Time-typed shard key raises 'requires String or Int64'. Range pruning handles only >=/<= pairs on the first key; other predicates scatter-gather. No spec for :time_range.

Probe on real SQLite shards: order(id).limit(3).offset(2) returned [4,6,7] (OFFSET applied per shard, not globally). sum/average/minimum/maximum raise 'No shard context'. shards_by __builder hard-codes DbType::Sqlite so PG/MySQL builds use the SQLite assembler. Specs use virtual adapters only, so merged real rows are unproven.

features.feature: Attribute API (virtual attributes, default values, converters)

features.gap: No store or store_accessor macro. serialized_column exists and could back it.

features.gap: No human_attribute_name or model_name object; error full_messages use raw attribute names.

features.gap: advanced_multi_database_spec.cr runs entirely on SQLite in-memory. There is no spec that registers a SQLite connection and a PostgreSQL connection in one process and drives two models against them (independent transactions, no cross-adapter placeholder or type leakage). compile_target_adapters_spec.cr proves only compile-time adapter selection.

Pool options are only asserted as URL query-string text (advanced_multi_database_spec 'builds pool URL'); no spec exercises checkout, exhaustion or DB::PoolTimeout, and PoolTimeout is not translated to a Grant error. build_pool_url never sets max_idle_pool_size, so crystal-db's default of 1 idle connection applies and a pool of 25 churns connections (open/close, TLS/auth handshake) under bursty load. No idle_timeout, reaper, min_connections or keepalive. Re-establishing a connection does not close the old pool (see disconnect row).

Only the healthy path of check_health_now is specced (SQLite in-memory). No spec for the unhealthy transition, timeout branch, recovery, the background loop, or get_adapter falling back when the monitor reports unhealthy. Defects by inspection: check_health uses an unbuffered Channel and, on the timeout branch, the spawned probe fiber later blocks forever on send (one leaked fiber per timeout); the model-level failover_retry_attempts and health_check_interval properties are stored but never read.

Specs prove role selection by adapter name and round-robin/strategy object construction, not that a query actually executes on a distinct replica (raw_sql_spec compares names; connection_handling_spec never opens a connection). Defects: configure_connection(load_balancing_strategy:) expands to an undefined load_balancing_strategy= setter (compile error); LeastConnectionsStrategy.release_connection is never called so counts only grow; re-establishing a :reading connection appends a duplicate replica; replica selection under get_adapter is not covered for the unhealthy-all fallback path.

Fiber-local connected_to(database/role/shard/prevent_writes) works. Missing versus AR 8: connects_to(database: {writing: :primary, reading: :replica}) hash form and a per-role pool config (only String/NamedTuple config: exists); connected_to(role: :reading) does not imply prevent_writes (AR does since 6.1); no connected_to? predicate, connected_to_many, connecting_to, or prohibit_shard_swapping (separate untracked rows).

requires_new semantics are inverted relative to AR: AR's requires_new: true opens a SAVEPOINT inside the outer transaction (rolled back with it), Grant opens a second physical connection that commits independently; transaction_spec asserts the inner row survives an outer raise (opposite of AR). Plain nested transaction in AR joins the parent (Rollback swallowed, nothing undone); Grant uses a savepoint. joinable: is absent. transaction is typed Nil and never returns the block value. On PG a requires_new write on rows the outer holds self-deadlocks; on SQLite it hits 'database is locked'. Suspected (not run): with a :reading role configured, BEGIN resolves via the role-aware adapter and can land on the replica, after which before_save's write mark makes Model.adapter resolve to the writer and writes escape the transaction.

The single savepoint spec covers one inner Rollback. Not covered: exception (non-Rollback) escaping an inner savepoint, after_commit/after_rollback pruning, savepoint failure on MySQL (unprepared path) or PG aborted-transaction state, and record-state restore at savepoint rollback. Default nesting is a savepoint here versus join-parent in AR (an AR Rollback in a plain nested block rolls nothing back). No manual create_savepoint/release_savepoint API.

spec/grant/transaction_spec.cr only asserts that each isolation symbol does not raise (its own comment says 'verify the API works'); no spec asserts the emitted BEGIN/SET TRANSACTION SQL or observable isolation. Nested transaction(isolation:) inside an open transaction silently ignores the option (AR raises TransactionIsolationError). SQLite maps levels onto BEGIN DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE (not real isolation) and ignores readonly. supports_isolation_level? returns true unconditionally on every adapter.

features.feature: Pessimistic locking (FOR UPDATE, FOR SHARE, SKIP LOCKED, NOWAIT)
features.gap: Specs cover SQL text per adapter and single-fiber with_lock on SQLite (where lock modes are a no-op); no spec proves blocking, NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED behavior on a real PG/MySQL server. Defects by inspection: with_lock does result.not_nil!, so a block returning nil raises; lock!/with_lock silently overwrite unsaved changes (AR raises 'Locking a record with unsaved changes is not supported'); NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED failures surface as raw DB::Error because LockNotAvailableError/LockWaitTimeoutError are never raised; lock accepts only the 6-value enum (no free-form lock string, no lock(false)); with_lock takes no transaction options.

Update path is guarded and specced (12 examples pass on SQLite). Not implemented: destroy of a stale record does not raise StaleObjectError (AR checks lock_version on destroy); no lock_optimistically toggle or locking_enabled?; touch/update_columns/update_all interplay unspecced. Opt-in via include Grant::Locking::Optimistic (a deliberate Crystal difference, fine) but it force-adds a lock_version column. Configurable column is tracked separately.

features.feature: Adapter feature matrix (PG vs MySQL vs SQLite differences)
features.gap: Only three capability predicates exist (supports_lock_mode?, supports_isolation_level?, supports_savepoints?) and the first two return true on PG. spec/adapter/adapters_spec.cr tests legacy Grant::Connections registration, not a feature matrix. A published per-adapter support table (and the ~25 AR supports_* predicates, see untracked row) is missing.

Restated: crystal-db already caches prepared statements per connection (StringKeyCache in lib/db/src/db/connection.cr) and honors prepared_statements / prepared_statements_cache URL parameters, so the row's 'no cache exists' is inaccurate. What is missing is Grant-level control and evidence: ConnectionSpec has no prepared_statements/cache option (only a hand-edited URL passes through build_pool_url), no statement_limit (the driver cache is an unbounded Hash), and no spec. Needed for PgBouncer transaction pooling (prepared_statements=false) and to bound memory when Sanitization inlines literals or IN lists vary in length.

Adapter#open_pool_connection wraps IO::Error and 'client was disconnected' into DB::ConnectionLost and relies on crystal-db's database.retry (retry_attempts default 1). No spec kills a connection and asserts recovery, no distinction between idempotent (safe to retry) and non-idempotent statements, and an in-flight transaction is not retried or reported as lost. No Grant-level ConnectionFailed/ConnectionNotEstablished error types.

Connection-context and virtual-shard routing specs pass on mocks/SQLite; no PostgreSQL or MySQL multi-database shard integration, and no spec where two shards resolve to two real physical databases with per-shard reader routing.

features.feature: Postgres transaction atomicity and same-connection writes

features.gap: Model.transaction and Base#transaction are declared `: Nil`; AR returns the block's value (e.g. `order = Order.transaction { ... create! }`).

No joinable: option; nested blocks always create savepoints, so AR code that relies on a plain nested block joining the parent (and Rollback being swallowed without undoing) or on joinable: false for transactional test wrappers behaves differently.
Setting isolation: on a nested (joined or savepoint) transaction is silently ignored instead of raising.

BEGIN is sent immediately on every transaction block, even ones that run no query or only reads that a cache satisfies; AR defers BEGIN until the first statement. Deferred: Low value, effort L, and lazy checkout mid-block risks starving the pool. Revisit after T01 lands and benchmarks show empty-transaction cost.

features.feature: Current transaction object and per-transaction callbacks (Rails 7.2)
features.gap: Model.current_transaction returns the internal TransactionState (no spec references it); there is no public Transaction#after_commit/after_rollback registration, open?/closed?, or isolation reader. The global after_all_transactions_commit is tracked separately.

Transactions are class methods on a model, so a service touching raw SQL or several models on one database must borrow an arbitrary model class. Grant.connection(name) (raw facade) has no transaction method.
Only block-form transactions exist; there is no explicit begin/commit/rollback or named savepoint API for connection-level code (rare, mostly used by test harnesses and libraries).
No helper that opens a joinable:false transaction around each example and rolls it back, across all registered connections. The suite instead clears tables.

features.feature: Row-lock unsaved-changes guard (lock! / with_lock on a dirty record)
features.gap: reload_with_lock copies fresh values over every column, silently discarding unsaved changes; AR raises RuntimeError 'Locking a record with unsaved changes is not supported'.

features.feature: Relation#lock with a custom SQL clause or false
features.gap: Grant's lock takes only the 6-value LockMode enum. There is no free-form vendor lock string (e.g. 'FOR NO KEY UPDATE', MySQL 'LOCK IN SHARE MODE') and no lock(false) to clear a lock inherited from a scope.

features.feature: Constraint-violation exception mapping (RecordNotUnique, InvalidForeignKey, NotNullViolation, ValueTooLong)
features.gap: Driver errors surface as raw DB::Error / PG::ResultError. Nothing translates unique, foreign-key, not-null or length violations (SQLSTATE 23505/23503/23502/22001, MySQL 1062/1452/1048, SQLite constraint text), so rescue-based patterns like create_or_find_by cannot be written portably.

features.feature: Statement failure wrapper carrying sql and binds (StatementInvalid)
features.gap: Errors do not carry the failing SQL or bind values; debugging requires the SQL debug log.

features.feature: Lock/timeout exception translation (Deadlocked, LockWaitTimeout, StatementTimeout, QueryCanceled, SerializationFailure)
features.gap: Deadlock and serialization failures are mapped, by message regex, only when raised inside a Model.transaction block (handle_transaction_error); outside a transaction they stay raw. LockWaitTimeoutError and LockNotAvailableError exist but are never raised for NOWAIT/lock-timeout. No StatementTimeout or QueryCanceled. Detection is message-text based, which is locale- and version-fragile.

features.feature: Connection/pool error types (ConnectionTimeoutError, ConnectionNotEstablished, ConnectionFailed, NoDatabaseError)
features.gap: Only AdapterNotAvailableError (a good actionable message, specced) exists. DB::PoolTimeout, connection refused and unknown-database errors are not mapped to Grant types; ConnectionNotEstablished is covered only by AdapterNotAvailableError semantics.
No Grant-level pool introspection. crystal-db exposes DB::Database#pool.stats (open, idle, in_flight, max), unused by Grant, and ConnectionRegistry.health_status reports only healthy/unhealthy.

features.feature: Pool disconnect and teardown (disconnect!, clear_all_connections!, remove_connection)
features.gap: No adapter close/disconnect exists anywhere in src. ConnectionRegistry.clear_all and re-establish_connection drop the Adapter reference without closing its DB::Database pool, leaking sockets and (for SQLite) file handles; the spec titled 'closes existing pool when re-establishing connection' only checks the new URL.

features.feature: Checked-out connection block (with_connection / lease_connection / permanent lease)
features.gap: Adapter#open yields a raw DB::Connection and is transaction/tenant-aware, but it is an internal API: Grant::Connection has no with_connection that pins ONE connection across a block (needed for session state such as SET LOCAL, temp tables, advisory locks, LISTEN). Only Transaction and SchemaTenant pin.

features.feature: Pool idle/reaper settings (idle_timeout, reaping_frequency, min_connections, keepalive)
features.gap: ConnectionSpec exposes pool_size, initial_pool_size, checkout_timeout, retry_attempts, retry_delay and health check timing only. crystal-db has max_idle_pool_size but no time-based idle reaping; Grant adds no reaper, so server-side idle connection kills (PgBouncer, cloud proxies) produce lost-connection errors on the next checkout.

features.feature: Connection liveness API (active?, verify!, reconnect!, connected?)
features.gap: HealthMonitor#check_health_now performs SELECT 1 per adapter (healthy path specced) and ConnectionRegistry.connection_exists? tests registration, but adapters have no public active?/reconnect!/verify! and models have no connected?.

features.feature: Database URL / DATABASE_URL configuration and adapter inference from URL scheme
features.gap: establish_connection requires the adapter class explicitly; the URL scheme (postgres://, mysql://, sqlite3:) is never used to choose one and DATABASE_URL is not read. Custom adapter registration by name (ConnectionAdapters.register) does not exist either.

features.feature: Database configurations API (db_config, configs_for, per-environment named configs)
features.gap: There is no config object model (HashConfig/UrlConfig equivalent) or lookup by environment/name; settings live only as ConnectionRegistry specs keyed by 'db:role[:shard]'. Loading a database.yml-shaped file is left to the app (Amber's environment YAML).

Equivalent operations exist only on ConnectionRegistry (establish_connection, connection_exists?, get_adapter) and Model.adapter/connection; models have no establish_connection, remove_connection, connected?, or connection_pool accessor.
No predicate to test the active role/shard; callers read current_role/current_shard and compare by hand.

connected_to applies to one model class's context; there is no way to switch several abstract classes (multi-database apps with ApplicationRecord and AnalyticsRecord) in one block, nor connecting_to for setting the role/shard without a block.
Nothing stops nested code from calling connected_to(shard:) inside a request already pinned to a tenant shard, so a stray shard switch can leak cross-tenant data.

connected_to(role: :reading) only switches the adapter; a write inside it is sent to the reader unless the caller also passes prevent_writes: true. prevent_writes_spec.cr covers the explicit flag only.

features.feature: Adapter capability predicates (supports_partial_index?, supports_json?, supports_insert_returning?, supports_ddl_transactions?, ...)
features.gap: Only supports_lock_mode?, supports_isolation_level?, supports_savepoints? and supports_index_hints? exist (pessimistic_spec checks the first). Missing: supports_insert_returning?, supports_insert_on_duplicate_skip?/update?, supports_ddl_transactions?, supports_partial_index?, supports_expression_index?, supports_check_constraints?, supports_foreign_keys?, supports_views?, supports_datetime_with_precision?, supports_json?, supports_common_table_expressions?, supports_virtual_columns?, supports_comments?, supports_explain?, supports_optimizer_hints?, supports_advisory_locks?, supports_bulk_alter?, supports_concurrent_connections?, supports_restart_db_transaction?, supports_disable_referential_integrity?, supports_nulls_not_distinct?.

features.feature: Adapter identity and server info (adapter_name, database_version, current_database, raw_connection)
features.gap: Adapters expose only postgres?/mysql?/sqlite? and name (the registry key). No adapter_name, server version (needed for feature gating), current database, or supported raw handle accessor.

features.feature: SQLite adapter defaults and PRAGMA configuration (foreign_keys, journal_mode, busy_timeout, synchronous)
features.gap: src/adapter/sqlite.cr sets no PRAGMAs, so foreign_keys is OFF (declared foreign keys are not enforced, unlike AR) and busy_timeout is 0 (a second pool connection writing gets 'database is locked' immediately). The sqlite3 driver accepts foreign_keys, journal_mode, busy_timeout, synchronous as URL parameters (lib/sqlite3/src/sqlite3/connection.cr) but Grant neither documents nor defaults them.

There is no per-connection variables hook, so statement_timeout, lock_timeout, application_name, default search_path and MySQL sql_mode cannot be set declaratively; no per-query timeout. MySQL adapter only forces utf8mb4 encoding. Deferred: crystal-db has no on-connect hook, so this needs an upstream or wrapped-connection factory. A SET on every checkout would double round trips.
Adapters implement clear(table) (DELETE; MySQL TRUNCATE) only. No disable_referential_integrity block, multi-table truncate, or sequence reset (PG DELETE does not reset SERIAL/BIGSERIAL).

features.feature: Literal question-mark escaping in raw SQL fragments
features.gap: PG ensure_clause_template rewrites every '?' to $n, including a '?' inside a quoted literal or the JSONB existence operator, shifting all later parameters; there is no escape syntax.
SQL logging exists (Instrumentation area) but there are no transaction-level events with outcome (commit/rollback/restart) for APM or slow-transaction detection.

Closed and exclusive-end ranges work (Q-6). Beginless (..5) and endless (5..) ranges raise ArgumentError 'Operator :gteq does not support nil values' from the assembler (reproduced on SQLite with where(id: ..5)). AR emits <= 5 / >= 5. Also unspecced: Time/Float/String ranges and Range inside Array.

Builder#merge appends where_fields, so where(a: 1).merge(where(a: 2)) yields a=1 AND a=2; AR replaces same-column equality conditions (last wins). Accepts only another Builder (no Hash/Proc). Named-scope merge conflicts, unscope-of-other, and select/from merge are unspecced. Existing specs live in modifiers/advanced_query/distinct, not in the row's original query_regressions_spec.cr (which has no merge example).

Supports :where(all), :order, :limit, :offset, :group, :having, :joins, :select, :distinct, :lock. Missing vs AR: unscope(where: :column) to drop only one column's predicates, :includes/:preload/:eager_load, :from, :readonly, :annotate, :optimizer_hints, :extending, :reordering, :with, :create_with.

features.feature: extending (adding methods to a relation at runtime)
features.not_applicable_reason: Ruby extends relation instances with arbitrary modules at runtime; Crystal uses static types and compile-time extensions.

features.gap: Only class-level Model.find_by/find_by! exist. Builder does not respond to find_by/find_by! (compile-time responds_to? probe on Parent.where(...) returned false), so Post.where(active: true).find_by(email: x) does not compile. AR relations and scopes support it. Composite/hash-arg forms fine at class level.

Builder#find_each supports batch_size/start/finish/order. Missing: cursor: (composite/non-PK cursor, Rails 7.1+), error_on_ignore:, and the block-less form returning an Enumerator/Iterator. Class-level Model.find_each has different signature and default (batch_size 100 with offset paging vs Builder 1000 with PK cursor), an inconsistency that can page with OFFSET on large tables.
Same as find_each: no cursor:, error_on_ignore:, no block-less enumerator form; Model-level variant uses OFFSET paging.

Grant's in_batches yields Array(Model), not a Relation, so batch.update_all / batch.delete_all / batch.pluck (AR's main use of in_batches) are unavailable even though the doc header shows batch.update_all. load: and error_on_ignore: parameters are accepted but ignored; cursor: missing; no block-less form. The row title claims 'relation-based'.

features.feature: select / custom column projection (SELECT id, name FROM ...)

features.gap: Builder exposes only group_by (Symbol, Array(Symbol), hash form); AR's canonical name group is absent (responds_to?(:group) false). String/expression group args (group('date(created_at)')) unsupported. group_by shadows Enumerable#group_by(&block) which is a semantic hazard.

rewhere clears ALL where_fields then applies the new conditions; AR only replaces predicates on the same columns and keeps others (where(a:1,b:2).rewhere(a:3) => b=2 AND a=3 in AR, only a=3 in Grant). reorder lacks String/Array/nil forms (reorder(nil) to clear). reverse_order on an unordered relation is a no-op (AR reverses the implicit primary-key order). rewhere accepts only **kwargs.

Supported: joins(table, on:), joins(:assoc), joins(:a, :b) incl. has_many :through (Q-15). Missing vs AR: raw SQL fragment joins('INNER JOIN ...'), nested association joins (joins(posts: :comments)), joins with a block/Arel node, self-join aliasing, polymorphic belongs_to joins, joins on associations with scope lambdas, and de-duplication when the same join is requested twice via different paths.
Grant only defines left_joins; the AR name left_outer_joins is absent (responds_to? false) and no spec uses it. Same raw-string and nested-hash gaps as joins.

WhereChain#has/#missing still require table:, foreign_key: keyword args and ignore the association name. No spec anywhere exercises where.has or where.missing. AR's public name is where.associated (Grant's has is not an AR API). Builder now has resolve_association_join (used by joins(:assoc)), so the association-name form is unblocked but not wired. missing should not need a foreign-key null test on joined rows when the association is through/composite.

features.feature: aggregations (count / sum / avg / min / max; Model.count returns Int64)
features.gap: count takes no column argument (no count(:col), count(:all), count(distinct: :col)); grouped count works but sum/avg/min/max ignore GROUP BY (group_by(:name).sum(:id) returned scalar 0.0 in a scratch probe instead of a Hash); sum returns Float64 for every column (precision loss on BIGINT/DECIMAL, AR returns Integer/BigDecimal; none-relation sum is 0.0 not 0); sum/avg ignore having/limit and IN-list chunking is only applied to count/ids. sum(&block)/Enumerable overloads absent.
Named aggregates exist; calculate(:count/:sum/:average/:minimum/:maximum, column) is absent (responds_to? false on relation and model).

features.not_applicable_reason: tally_by is not an ActiveRecord 8 public API.

features.feature: readonly relations (prevent persistence on fetched records)
features.gap: No Relation#readonly / unscope(:readonly). Record-level readonly!/readonly? and ReadOnlyRecordError exist (transactions.cr; spec/grant/persistence_helpers_spec.cr) so only the relation flag that marks each hydrated record is missing.

features.feature: optimizer hints (e.g. FORCE INDEX for MySQL)
features.gap: Index hints exist: use_index/force_index/ignore_index with adapter index_hint_clause and Grant.settings.index_hint_mode fallback (src/grant/scale/index_hints.cr). The AR optimizer_hints('MAX_EXECUTION_TIME(1000)') comment-hint API (/*+ ... */ for MySQL, pg_hint_plan on PG, SQLite ignored) is absent.

Not re-run on PG (out of scope). Builder has load_async, async_count/sum/avg/min/max/pluck/delete/update. Missing: async_ids, async_pick, async_exists?, async_find_by_sql, async_average alias, and a global async executor/config (AR config.active_record.async_query_executor). Original PG note (zero results, empty metrics) unverified here.

sole exists on relation and model; find_sole_by only at class level (Builder does not respond to it), same relation-level finder gap as find_by. The original three evidence paths do not mention sole; convenience_methods_spec.cr does.

features.feature: WhereChain (LIKE, NOT LIKE, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, NOT IN, BETWEEN, comparison ops, EXISTS/NOT EXISTS)

features.gap: No Model.cache/uncached block or per-request (Amber pipe) query cache. Writes must clear it.

features.feature: from (custom FROM clause / subquery as table)
features.gap: No Relation#from(source, subquery_name = nil) (responds_to? false); no unscope(:from).

features.feature: Relation take / first / last result helpers
features.gap: (1) Builder has first, first(n), last, first!, last! but no take/take(n) (only Model.take; relation responds_to?(:take) false) and no last(n). (2) first, first(n) and any? MUTATE the receiver: after rel.first, rel.raw_sql contains ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 1 (reproduced with a scratch spec), so a later rel.select returns one row; AR never mutates. (3) Composite-PK models order by primary_name only. (4) Unordered relations otherwise get an implicit ORDER BY pk DESC in the assembler, unlike AR.

Builder#destroy_all loads all matching records then calls destroy on each (Int32 count). Specs only assert the returned count on SQLite (convenience_methods_spec.cr) and the empty case; no spec proves before/after_destroy callbacks or dependent: handling fire for relation destroy_all; original evidence path persistence/delete_spec.cr does not reference destroy_all. Returns Int32 (records) while delete_all returns Int64. Not verified on PG/MySQL.

features.feature: Relation immutability (each chain method returns a new relation)
features.gap: Every Builder chain method (where, order, limit, etc.) mutates and returns self. base = Post.where(a: 1); base.where(b: 2); base.where(c: 3) accumulates b and c on base. Named scopes and Model.current_scope hide this in the common path, but reused/stored relations (helper methods, memoized filters, terminal first/any?) leak state.

features.feature: all returns a lazy Relation (Model.all / relation.all)
features.gap: Model.all and Builder#all execute the query and return Array(Model). AR returns a chainable Relation (Post.all.where(...), Post.all.includes(...) before loading). Builder includes Enumerable so iteration works, but chaining after all does not.

features.feature: Relation load / loaded? / reset / records memoization
features.gap: Builder re-executes SQL on every each/to_a/size; no memoized records, load, loaded?, reset, reload, records (all responds_to? false).

features.feature: second / third / fourth / fifth / forty_two / second_to_last / third_to_last (and ! forms)
features.gap: None defined on Builder or Model (responds_to? false).

features.feature: Relation-level finders (find with ids/array, find_by, find_by!, find_sole_by, find_or_create_by, find_or_initialize_by, create_or_find_by)
features.gap: Builder#find(id) is only Crystal's Enumerable#find (block/ifnone), not AR find(id); find(array_of_ids) and find(*ids) return nothing at model level either. find_or_create_by/find_or_initialize_by exist on Model only (integrators.cr), never on a relation, so where(x: 1).find_or_create_by(y: 2) does not apply the scope attributes. create_or_find_by absent.

features.feature: Relation build / create / create! / new with scope attributes, create_with, scope_attributes
features.gap: Builder has no create/build/new (responds_to? false); create_with absent; where_values_hash absent. Scope-derived attributes (Post.where(published: true).build) are not applied.
Only update_all (SQL, no callbacks) exists on Builder; no Relation#update(attrs) or update(id, attrs) running validations and callbacks per record (responds_to? false).

features.feature: many? / one? / none? / empty? efficient existence-count predicates
features.gap: any? uses SQL; many? is absent (responds_to? false); one?/none?/empty? on Builder resolve to Enumerable and iterate/load every row; any? mutates the receiver with LIMIT 1.
No only(*components)/except(*components); unscope covers a subset of except.
Absent. AR 7+/8 in_order_of(:col, values, filter: true) also filters to the given values.
Absent (Post.where(...).extract_associated(:author)).
Absent (Post.excluding(post1, post2)).
Absent.
Only Grant's non-AR where.has(association, table:, foreign_key:) exists; the AR spelling where.associated(:assoc) is absent (see where.missing / where.has row).

features.feature: where with nested table hash / joined-table columns / record values
features.gap: structured_field_sql only accepts columns present in Model.fields, so joined-table columns in a hash fail with 'Unknown query field'; nested hash form and where(association: record) / where(fk: record) not supported.
Only positional ? binds; :name named binds unsupported in Builder#where and sanitize_sql_array (grep of sanitization.cr finds no named handling).

features.feature: where.not with hash / multi-condition (NAND) and non-scalar values
features.gap: WhereChain#not(field, value) accepts one scalar pair. AR where.not(a: 1, b: 2) (NOT (a=1 AND b=2)), arrays (NOT IN), nil (IS NOT NULL), ranges are unsupported via the keyword form (the block form exists).

features.feature: or / and with a relation argument and structural-compatibility check
features.gap: Post.where(a: 1).or(Post.where(b: 2)) form absent; only flat kw/string or and block or. AR raises ArgumentError for structurally incompatible relations (differing joins/limit/etc.).

features.feature: select with raw SQL expressions, aliases and block form
features.gap: select accepts only Symbols (Builder#select(*columns : Symbol)); select('COUNT(*) AS n'), aliased computed columns and reading them from records have no path (AR exposes extra attributes via attributes/[]). Block form is Enumerable-like only.

features.feature: order with raw SQL / expressions / NULLS FIRST-LAST
features.gap: order accepts only column symbols with :asc/:desc; no order('lower(name) DESC'), no nulls_first/nulls_last, no expression ordering, no order on joined-table column.
Only count honors group_fields (Q-12). group_by(:name).sum(:id) returned scalar 0.0 in a scratch probe (GROUP BY silently ignored by the sum path in aggregations.cr), a silent wrong-result hazard.

features.feature: pluck / pick typed results and SQL expressions
features.gap: Results are Array(Array(Grant::Columns::Type)) (untyped union, needs casts); no pluck('COUNT(*)') or expression pluck; no pluck on joined-table columns by qualified name in the public overload.

The assembler adds ORDER BY pk DESC to any unordered SELECT (verified: Parent.where(name: 'a').raw_sql ends with ORDER BY id DESC); AR emits no ORDER BY for all/where and orders by pk ASC only for first/last/find_each. No implicit_order_column macro/setting.
Only unscoped { } exists; no scoping { } that makes a relation the current scope for the block (responds_to? false).

features.not_applicable_reason: references exists so includes can guess JOIN vs preload by parsing string conditions at runtime; Grant selects the strategy explicitly (includes/preload/eager_load).

features.gap: Absent (responds_to? false); no WITH clause support in the assemblers.

WhereChain offers string-field predicates (where.gt(:age, 18)) but no typed column objects that compose (Post.arel_table[:id].gt(1).and(...)), no OR-ing of predicates, no reuse across where/order/select/having/joins conditions. Deferred: Effort L. Its value depends on stable relation immutability (Q01) and where composition (Q02). Consider a typed-column design in a later release, not this program.
raw_sql exists (functionally to_sql) but to_sql is absent; cache_key/cache_version (collection cache keys from COUNT + MAX(updated_at)) absent.
Deferred: Low value and effort M. Merge with Cross-database associations (has_many / has_one through with disable_joins: true), which is a duplicate. Revisit after A02.

Read side works (lazy, eager preload A-14, delete_all of join rows A-15). Write side is absent: <<, append and delete raise ArgumentError on a through collection (probe P5), build/create produce the target with no join row (probe P5b: 0 join rows), no <tag>_ids= is generated for through, and only a single through hop is resolvable (through_associations does one registry lookup). Deferred: Low value and effort M. Merge with Cross-database associations (has_many / has_one through with disable_joins: true), which is a duplicate. Revisit after A02.

Preloading is silently wrong: PrbOwner.includes(:prb_badge) marks the association loaded but the value is nil while the lazy reader returns the record (probe P7), because _eager_batch_load treats the annotation as a plain has_one and ignores through. The through: option takes the intermediate TABLE name (SQL is built from through.id.stringify, parity spec passes through: :parity_accounts for association parity_account), not the association name as in AR. No setter, no eager_load JOIN, only a single hop, no scope support.
No has_and_belongs_to_many macro. Depends on has_many :through writers, which are also absent, so HABTM cannot be built from existing pieces yet.

(1) Primary keys must be Int64/Int32: the setter raises for UUID/String keys and load_polymorphic takes Int64. (2) has_many/has_one `as:` carry no @[Grant::Relationship] annotation, so includes/preload of them is a silent no-op (probe Q2: association_loaded? false). (3) has_one as: has no setter (probe Q4), no result caching, no inverse_of. (4) dependent supports only :destroy and :nullify; :delete_all, :delete, :restrict_* are silently ignored. (5) The type column stores record.class.name / self.class.name, not the STI base class (AR polymorphic_name). (6) Polymorphic associations are not registered in AssociationRegistry. (7) has_many as: returns LoadedAssociationCollection that hydrates all rows on every access and filters where() in memory.

The spellings already match AR (has_many :delete_all, has_one :delete), and dependent_delete_all_spec.cr covers both (ran: pass). Remaining: dependent: :destroy_async (and ensuring_owner_was) is absent; any unrecognized dependent: value (e.g. has_many :delete, :restrict_with_error) falls through the macro elsif chain and is silently ignored (probe P3); dependent is not applied on has_many :through join rows.

Code has closed part of the tracked gap: :restrict_with_exception is implemented (raises Grant::Associations::RestrictError) and tested in association_parity_spec.cr. Still absent: the AR name :restrict_with_error is not recognized and is silently ignored (probe P3: destroy returned true and deleted the owner); Grant's :restrict is a non-AR alias. The exception class is RestrictError, not a DeleteRestrictionError-named equivalent; the error message is added to :base only.

New and dirty (autosave: true) children are saved via after_save with save!, so an invalid child raises after the owner row is written (inside the around_save transaction) instead of owner.save returning false with an error on the owner (AR validate: true default). No autosave: false semantics, no mark_for_destruction/marked_for_destruction?, no per-child has_many replace/removal on save, and the belongs_to autosave only saves unpersisted parents.

Create/destroy/FK-change adjustments work (regressions A-10, A-17, options spec) and a polymorphic counter cache exists (integration_spec), but: reset_counters and increment_counter/decrement_counter class helpers are absent (update_counters exists); counter_cache: true derives the column with a naive `underscore + "s_count"` (Category -> categorys_count, AR gives categories_count); conditional counter_cache: {active: false} unsupported; has_many counter_cache: option (so size reads the cached column) unsupported; collection delete/delete_all/clear do not decrement; in-memory parent counters are not updated; polymorphic counter cache requires Int64 ids.

setup_touch runs after_save/after_destroy on the current parent only (self.association). When the FK changes, AR also touches the previous parent; Grant does not. No spec covers touch on destroy or the old-parent case. Touch runs one UPDATE per save even when nothing changed.

Verified defects: (1) the association scope lambda is ignored on preload (probe Q1: lazy returns 1 published post, includes returns 2); (2) has_one :through preload is silently nil (probe P7); (3) polymorphic has_many/has_one as: are never preloaded (probe Q2); (4) includes(:typo) raises nothing (probe Q3), AR raises AssociationNotFoundError; (5) nesting deeper than one level does not compile (Hash(Symbol, Array(Symbol)) type; includes(a: {b: :c}) is a type error in builder.cr); (6) includes never switches to a JOIN when a where condition references the association table (needs explicit eager_load); (7) eager_load raises for polymorphic and unresolved through.

Record and relation flags work (A-19), but the only spec wraps its assertions in `if responds_to?` guards. Missing: association-level `strict_loading: true` option, class-level strict_loading_by_default, strict_loading_mode :n_plus_one_only, strict_loading!(mode) argument, propagation of the flag to records loaded through a strict owner's association, and a configurable action (raise vs log). The has_one/belongs_to generated readers assert, but has_one as: and has_many as: do only when not loaded and skip propagation.

Only has_many and has_one are handled (source branches on :has_many/:has_one); belongs_to nested attributes are unsupported. reject_if accepts only :all_blank; a proc is silently treated as nil. No index_errors, no RecordNotFound when an id is not part of the association, and it needs an explicit `enable_nested_saves` call plus a typed declaration (acceptable Crystal idiom). Spec covers create/update/destroy/limit/update_only/all_blank/validation propagation for has_many and has_one only.
No delegated_type macro. Everything it needs (polymorphic belongs_to, has_one as:, enum-style predicates) exists separately, but only for Int64 keys.

Zero-argument scope lambda works for has_many (expression body only: the macro splices `q.{{scope.body}}`), but it is ignored by preload (probe Q1), by dependent:, and is unsupported on belongs_to/has_one. No extend: module or block form, and no instance-dependent scope (lambda receiving the owner).

<singular>_ids and <singular>_ids= are generated for non-through has_many (irregular plurals via singular:). Gaps: not generated for has_many :through or has_many as:; the writer does not raise for ids that do not exist (AR raises RecordNotFound; here find returns nil and the id is silently skipped), ignores blank ids no differently, is not wrapped in a transaction, saves each record individually, and the reader hydrates all records (`all.map`) instead of plucking ids when not loaded. Reader returns Array(Columns::Type), not typed ids.

On a through collection build/create skip the join row entirely (probe P5b). create on an unsaved owner saves an orphan with a NULL FK (AR raises RecordNotSaved). build does not set the inverse association, has no block form, and takes only named args (no Hash or Array of attribute hashes). Built records are only tracked when the collection was already loaded.

delete_all always issues DELETE on target rows (non-through) and delete/clear always nullify the FK, whereas AR follows the association's dependent strategy: default for has_many is :nullify for delete_all, :destroy/:delete_all when configured, and join-row deletion for through. delete_all(dependent) argument absent. destroy_all returns Int32 rather than the destroyed records.

Only record-level association_loaded?(name) and clear_loaded_associations (all at once) exist. No per-association reset/reload, no collection loaded?/reload/reset/load_target, and Base#reload does not clear the association cache (probe P2: association_loaded? still true after reload). Specs only assert association_loaded? after eager loading; nothing tests reset.

AssociationRegistry.get(class_name, name) returns type, target_class, foreign_key, primary_key, through, source, and it is spec'd for belongs_to/has_many/has_one through. Missing: enumerate all associations of a model, macro/collection?/polymorphic?/klass/through_reflection/source_reflection/inverse_of/options/class_name accessors, and polymorphic associations are never registered (only a class_getter meta) so the registry cannot describe them. Registry is keyed by class-name String and returns a NamedTuple.

features.feature: belongs_to validates the referenced record, not only foreign-key presence
singular association builders build_<assoc> / create_<assoc> / create_<assoc>!

features.feature: stale-target detection when a belongs_to/has_one foreign key changes
